What is the formula for the total surface area of a hemisphere of radius r?

What is the formula for the total surface area of a hemisphere of radius r?
questions.a:
3πr². A wrong answer like 2πr² shows the student forgot to include the flat circular base, confusing curved surface area with total surface area – a common error when visualizing hemispheres as "half" without considering the exposed base.

questions.q:
Why is the surface area of a sphere not simply twice the area of a circle (2 × πr²)?

Why is the surface area of a sphere not simply twice the area of a circle (2 × πr²)?
questions.a:
Because a sphere’s surface curves in all three dimensions, not just flat like two circles. The formula 4πr² comes from integrating infinitesimal rings over the sphere’s surface, which yields four times the area of a great circle. A wrong answer like "it is 2πr²" reveals the student is applying 2D logic (stacking circles) to a 3D object without understanding how surface accumulates in three dimensions.

questions.q:
A spherical laddoo has a radius of 4.2 cm. Calculate its surface area. Use π = 22/7.

A spherical laddoo has a radius of 4.2 cm. Calculate its surface area. Use π = 22/7.
questions.a:
Step 1: Radius r = 4.2 cm  
Step 2: Formula for sphere surface area = 4πr²  
Step 3: r² = 4.2 × 4.2 = 17.64 cm²  
Step 4: 4 × (22/7) × 17.64 = 4 × 22 × 2.52 = 88 × 2.52 = 221.76 cm²  
Step 5: Final answer = 221.76 cm²  
A wrong answer like 55.44 cm² suggests the student used 2πr² (hemisphere curved area) or forgot to square the radius properly – indicating confusion between sphere and hemisphere formulas or incorrect order of operations.

questions.q:
Two hemispheres of radius 5 cm are joined base-to-base to form a sphere. Is the total surface area of the resulting sphere equal to the sum of the total surface areas of the two separate hemispheres? Explain.

Two hemispheres of radius 5 cm are joined base-to-base to form a sphere. Is the total surface area of the resulting sphere equal to the sum of the total surface areas of the two separate hemispheres? Explain.
questions.a:
No. Each hemisphere has total surface area 3πr² = 3π(25) = 75π cm², so two separate have 150π cm². When joined, the two bases are internal and not part of the outer surface. The sphere’s surface area is 4πr² = 100π cm². The two bases (each πr² = 25π) are lost, so 150π - 2×25π = 100π cm². A wrong answer like "yes, they are equal" shows the student fails to recognize that joining surfaces removes shared faces from the total external area – a critical 3D spatial reasoning error.

questions.q:
A student calculates the surface area of a hemisphere of radius 14 cm as 2 × (22/7) × 14 × 14 = 1232 cm². Is this correct? Identify the error and give the right answer.

A student calculates the surface area of a hemisphere of radius 14 cm as 2 × (22/7) × 14 × 14 = 1232 cm². Is this correct? Identify the error and give the right answer.
questions.a:
Incorrect. The student computed 2πr², which is only the curved surface area. For total surface area of a hemisphere, we need curved surface (2πr²) plus base (πr²) = 3πr². Correct calculation: 3 × (22/7) × 14 × 14 = 3 × 22 × 2 × 14 = 3 × 616 = 1848 cm². A wrong justification like "the formula is 2πr²" reveals the student does not distinguish between curved and total surface area – a persistent mix-up in mensuration.

questions.a:
